scope.filter: AI and software-development posts with concrete tools, workflows, evidence, experiments, or useful criticism
scope.note: Replies and repost-only activity may not appear on logged-out public profile timelines. Off-topic and low-signal posts were omitted. Timestamps were derived from X status IDs.

items.summary: Used datasette-mcp to have a voice conversation with a Datasette backup of his blog through the ChatGPT iPhone app.
items.signal: Demonstrates a working personal-knowledge interface rather than merely describing one.

items.summary: Built an interactive UI for Gemini 3.8 TTS, including multi-speaker conversations and voice cloning, then used Claude to script a two-pelican dialogue.
items.signal: Ships a usable playground alongside the observation.

items.summary: Published notes and comparison grids for Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Sol, and GPT-6 Luna across reasoning levels.
items.signal: Side-by-side artifacts make the model-release commentary inspectable.

items.summary: Highlighted GPT-6 Luna's lower price and described it as his preferred model for product features because of cost and speed.
items.signal: Concrete deployment preference with explicit criteria.

items.summary: Suggested that DHH's recent work may have created a new wave of Rust programmers.
items.signal: A compact observation about agents changing the practical cost of adopting unfamiliar languages.

items.summary: Briefly endorsed cache warming in the context of current development tooling.
items.signal: Potentially useful operational note, though the public post lacks enough standalone context.

items.summary: Highlighted a Broforce-style game built in a few hours with Astra and published as a playable artifact.
items.signal: Points to a concrete, testable result rather than a capability claim.

items.summary: Recommended 'AI Has No Wisdom and Neither Will You,' arguing that teams stop reading and writing code at their peril.
items.signal: Useful counterweight to hands-off vibe-coding claims.

items.summary: Flagged that Claude Code 2.1.277 can silently skip a local AGENTS.md when telemetry or nonessential traffic is disabled because the loader is controlled by a remote feature flag.
items.signal: High-value operational edge case with direct consequences for local agent behavior.

items.summary: Expanded CodexBar support across a broad set of AI coding and inference providers and noted the removal of recurring keychain alerts.
items.signal: Concrete tooling update for monitoring multi-provider AI usage.

items.summary: Said the next OpenClaw version uses a decision model to choose automatically between steering and queueing, with API-compatible, local, and ONNX options.
items.signal: Specific architectural use of a small decision model inside an agent harness.

items.summary: Quoted a user's judgment that Amp is the strongest available harness.
items.signal: Anecdotal rather than measured, but relevant as practitioner feedback.

items.summary: Ran the same documentation-writing prompt through GPT-6 Sol, Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra High, and Fable 5.1 Ultra and shared the outputs.
items.signal: Comparable prompt and visible outputs make the model comparison auditable.

items.summary: Reported strong results from asking agents to test features end-to-end and provide irrefutable proof that they work, contrasting this with much of his historical unit-test effort.
items.signal: A directly reusable verification prompt and a concrete testing philosophy.

items.summary: Shared his personal recommendation for deciding where AI context belongs across documents, skills, memories, and related stores.
items.signal: Directly addresses a recurring practical problem in agent-system design; the attached visual contains the useful detail.

items.summary: Published a structured guide that routes humans and agents to the appropriate evaluation resources based on their problem.
items.signal: A practical index designed to reduce aimless searching.

items.summary: Defined AI evals as tests of whether a system does what its builders want, while distinguishing product evals from model benchmarks.
items.signal: Concise clarification of a distinction teams routinely blur.

items.summary: Called out bots replying to other bots as a growing firehose of low-quality content.
items.signal: Useful warning about automated engagement degrading feedback channels.

items.summary: Recommended installing the eval skills he created with Shreya Shankar and running /eval-audit against an existing pipeline to identify low-hanging improvements.
items.signal: Immediately actionable workflow backed by public tooling.

items.summary: Hosted a practical session testing whether Opus 5.5 reduces stereotypical AI writing slop.
items.signal: Frames model-quality discussion as an evaluation exercise rather than a vibe.

items.summary: Recommended running /claude-api prompt-audit in Claude Code to inspect skills, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and prompts for anti-patterns that hinder frontier models.
items.signal: Specific command, defined scope, and updated guidance for the current model.

items.summary: Suggested /claude-api migrate for application code and /claude-api prompt-audit for skills and prompts when moving to Opus 5.5.
items.signal: Concrete migration and validation workflow rather than release-day cheerleading.
